about: Scoring fixtures. Every `expect` block below was worked out by hand from the cost model in
src/score.js and then written down here, before the scorer was run against it. Two
independent implementations are held to these numbers: the JavaScript scorer, via
`node bin/recall.js fixtures`, and a separate Python reimplementation in
scripts/check_independent.py that shares no code with it.
The first case is the negative control and it must score zero. A scorer that always finds
something wrong passes every suite built only out of wrong answers, so a suite without a
perfect reconstruction in it proves nothing.

costModel.reversal: one structural edit, not a deletion plus an insertion

cases.name: perfect reconstruction scores zero
cases.reference:
graph TD
  Sun[Sunlight] --> Leaf[Leaf]
  Leaf -->|glucose| Growth[Growth]
  Water[Water] --> Leaf
cases.attempt:
graph TD
  Growth[Growth]
  Leaf[Leaf] -->|glucose| Growth
  Water[Water] --> Leaf
  Sun[Sunlight] --> Leaf
derivation: Same four nodes with the same captions and the same default shape.
Same three directed pairs with the same labels, written in a different order and with
the nodes declared in a different order. Statement order is not part of a graph, so
there is nothing to charge for. Distance 0.

cases.name: one reversed relation is one error and is named as such
cases.reference:
graph TD
  Hypothesis --> Experiment
  Experiment --> Result
cases.attempt:
graph TD
  Experiment --> Hypothesis
  Experiment --> Result
derivation: Nodes identical, so no node cost.
Experiment --> Result matches exactly.
Reference has Hypothesis --> Experiment and nothing matches it. The attempt has
Experiment --> Hypothesis and nothing matches that. Neither graph holds a second link
between the pair in the other direction, so this is one reversal, cost 1, and it is
reported once. Textbook graph edit distance would charge 2 here.
Structure 1, everything else 0.

cases.name: a reversal keeps its label when the label is right
cases.reference:
graph LR
  Rain -->|feeds| River
  River --> Sea
cases.attempt:
graph LR
  River -->|feeds| Rain
  River --> Sea
derivation: River --> Sea matches. Rain -->|feeds| River is reversed into River -->|feeds| Rain.
The reversal pass pairs them and then compares their attributes: both carry the label
"feeds", so there is no label cost. Structure 1, label 0.

cases.name: an added opposite link is an extra edge and NOT a reversal
cases.role: negative control for the reversal detector
cases.attempt:
graph TD
  A --> B
  B --> A
derivation: A --> B matches exactly, so the reference has nothing left over.
The reversal pass needs an unmatched reference link and finds none, so B --> A cannot
be a reversal of anything. It is one extra relation. Structure 1.
This case exists because a reversal detector that only looks for an opposing link,
without checking that the forward link went unmatched, calls this a reversal and
tells the learner they got backwards a relation they in fact got right.

cases.name: dropping one side of a two way pair is a missing edge, not a reversal
cases.role: negative control for the reversal detector
cases.reference:
graph TD
  A --> B
  B --> A
derivation: B --> A matches exactly. The reference's A --> B is left over, and the attempt has
nothing left over for it to pair with, so it is a plain missing relation.
Structure 1.

cases.name: two reversals are two errors
cases.reference:
graph TD
  A --> B
  B --> C
  C --> D
cases.attempt:
graph TD
  B --> A
  B --> C
  D --> C
derivation: B --> C matches. A --> B is reversed, C --> D is reversed. Two independent reversals,
one structural edit each. Structure 2.

cases.name: the shape is right and one link label is wrong
cases.reference:
graph LR
  Source -->|compiles to| Object
  Object -->|links to| Binary
cases.attempt:
graph LR
  Source -->|compiles to| Object
  Object -->|objects| Binary
derivation: Both relations exist and point the right way, so structure is 0.
One link label differs. Label 1. Total 1, and the report has to say the shape is
correct, because that is the difference between misremembering a word and not having
the model.

cases.name: a node caption is wrong and nothing else is
derivation: Same node ids, same relation, same direction. Structure 0.
One node caption differs. Label 1.

cases.name: structurally wrong: one relation missing and one invented
cases.reference:
graph TD
  A --> B
  B --> C
  C --> D
cases.attempt:
graph TD
  A --> B
  B --> C
  A --> D
derivation: A --> B and B --> C match. C --> D is missing. A --> D is extra, and it is not the
reverse of C --> D because it does not join the same pair. Two independent structural
edits. Structure 2.

cases.name: a missing node takes its relations with it
cases.reference:
graph TD
  A --> B
  B --> C
derivation: A --> B matches. Node C is absent: one node deletion.
B --> C cannot be placed because one endpoint is gone, so it is also deleted.
Structure 2.

cases.name: an arrow where the reference has a plain line
derivation: The pair is right and the claim about it is not. An undirected link and a directed
one have different structural keys, so nothing matches in the first pass, and the
directedness pass reports one edit. Structure 1.

cases.name: shape and line style are style, not structure
derivation: Same nodes, same captions, same relation, same direction. Structure 0, label 0.
A is a diamond in the reference and a rectangle in the attempt: style 1.
The link is dotted in the reference and solid in the attempt: style 1.
Style 2, total 2, and the report has to say the diagram claims the right thing.

cases.name: a reversal and a label error on different relations add up
cases.reference:
graph TD
  A -->|first| B
  B -->|second| C
cases.attempt:
graph TD
  B -->|first| A
  B -->|two| C
derivation: A -->|first| B is reversed and the label survives: structure 1, label 0 for it.
B --> C points the right way and its label is wrong: structure 0, label 1.
Structure 1, label 1, total 2.

cases.name: a node in the wrong subgraph is a grouping error
cases.reference:
graph TD
  subgraph Ingest
    A --> B
  end
  subgraph Serve
    C
  end
  B --> C
cases.attempt:
graph TD
  subgraph Ingest
    A --> B
    C
  end
  subgraph Serve
    D[Serve]
  end
  B --> C
derivation: Nodes A, B and C exist in both with the same captions and shapes.
The attempt adds node D, which the reference does not have: structure 1.
Both relations match. C sits in Serve in the reference and in Ingest in the attempt:
grouping 1. Structure 1, grouping 1, total 2.
The attempt uses an identifier the reference does not have, so the correspondence is
no longer given and the exact search runs. Four nodes is below the cap. The search
returns A->A, B->B, C->C with D inserted, which is the correspondence above.

cases.name: renamed nodes force a correspondence search
cases.reference:
graph TD
  A[Heat] --> B[Steam]
  B --> C[Turbine]
cases.attempt:
graph TD
  X[Heat] --> Y[Steam]
  Y --> Z[Turbine]
derivation: No attempt identifier exists in the reference, so the identity correspondence does not
apply and the search runs. Three nodes is below the exact cap, so branch and bound
finds A->X, B->Y, C->Z, under which every caption and every relation matches.
Distance 0, reported as exact.

cases.name: renamed nodes with one reversal still finds the reversal
cases.reference:
graph TD
  A[Heat] --> B[Steam]
  B --> C[Turbine]
cases.attempt:
graph TD
  Y[Steam] --> X[Heat]
  Y --> Z[Turbine]
derivation: The best correspondence is still A->X, B->Y, C->Z, because it makes every caption
agree and leaves only the Heat to Steam link turned round.
Under it, B --> C matches, and A --> B is reversed. Structure 1.
No other correspondence does better: any mapping that disagrees on a caption pays 1
for that caption and cannot save more than 1 on the links.

cases.name: above the exact cap the answer is an upper bound and says so
cases.reference:
graph TD
  A1[One] --> A2[Two]
  A2 --> A3[Three]
  A3 --> A4[Four]
  A4 --> A5[Five]
  A5 --> A6[Six]
  A6 --> A7[Seven]
  A7 --> A8[Eight]
  A8 --> A9[Nine]
  A9 --> A10[Ten]
cases.attempt:
graph TD
  B1[One] --> B2[Two]
  B2 --> B3[Three]
  B3 --> B4[Four]
  B4 --> B5[Five]
  B5 --> B6[Six]
  B6 --> B7[Seven]
  B7 --> B8[Eight]
  B8 --> B9[Nine]
  B9 --> B10[Ten]
derivation: Ten nodes, every identifier renamed, so the correspondence has to be searched and ten
is above the exact cap of eight. The bipartite heuristic runs instead.
Every caption is unique and appears in both graphs, so the assignment that pairs equal
captions costs nothing in the cost matrix and is the one the Hungarian solver picks.
Under it the two chains are identical, so the edit script it produces is empty and the
upper bound is 0. An upper bound of 0 pins the true distance at 0, since a distance
cannot be negative. The result is still reported with exact false and bound upper,
because the method cannot prove optimality in general and must not claim to.

cases.name: forcing the identity correspondence on renamed nodes rebuilds the whole graph
derivation: The identity correspondence is asked for explicitly, and no attempt identifier exists
in the reference, so nothing pairs up.
Two reference nodes deleted, two attempt nodes inserted: 4.
The reference link cannot be placed, and the attempt link has no counterpart: 2 more.
Structure 6, total 6. This is the honest cost of that correspondence, and it is why
auto does not choose it when the identifiers disagree.
